cases.name: Wendy Stephens (Jane Doe B-10)
cases.about: Please send information about her life, dreams or interests to shecounted@gmail.com
cases.narrative: On 3/21/1984, one of her bones was found by a dog who belonged to a little league baseball field manager, which led police to the rest of her remains on property that is now Sea-Tac International Airport. She remain unidentified as "Jane Doe B-10" or "Bones 10" until January 2021 when her remains were identified by genetic genealogy. Gary Leon Ridgway confessed to her murder while she still remained unidentified as "Bones 10."  In his confession before the court, he said, "In King County, Washington, sometime between January 1, 1982 through March 21, 1984, with premeditated intent to cause her death, I strangled an unidentified woman referred to as Jane Doe "B1O" to death. I picked her up, planning to kill her. After killing her, I left her body near the northern boundary of Sea-Tac Airport.

cases.name: Victoria Aparicio Cruz
cases.narrative:
He allegedly stabbed her at least 20 times. He is accused of using a filet knife, “slicing through her neck, slicing her hands in multiple places as she tried to defend herself, and stabbing her multiple times in the back even after she was clearly unresponsive and deceased.”

The documents states that "both women received neck wounds so large and deep it appears clear that the defendant was attempting to slice and saw at his victims, and not simply stab them." The court documents describe their fatal injuries as extremely violent, including "sawed" jugular and carotid veins, a partially-severed spinal cord, and postmortem stab wounds.
